newsitem.title: UK: UK says would consider more OFWAT powers if needed.
newsitem.headline: UK says would consider more OFWAT powers if needed.

text.p: The UK Government would be prepared to look at extra powers for water industry regulator OFWAT if needed to tackle mandatory leakage targets, deputy Prime Minister John Prescott told a news conference on Monday.
"We said we probably think there might be more that may be needed," Prescott said, adding that OFWAT head Ian Byatt had told the government he felt his powers were adequate.
"We will watch what happens over the summer," he said.

A 10-point plan was being presented to the water industry at an emergency conference on Monday to tackle the country's worst drought in 200 years. The plan includes a five year target to reduce leaks, and Prescott indicated that the regulator was working to set those targets.
Prescott added that he felt the regulator would have a "more hands on approach" on the issue of cutting leaks.
Environment Minister Michael Meacher suggested a level of leakage of 10-15 percent was generally seen as an economical target.
"We are pressing as hard as we can to get down to (a reasonable) level," he told the news conference.
Prescott said he wanted review the situation in the autumn, probably with another conference. He also said that a review of tariff structures would look at all possibilities.
